h: Red squirrels, mountain air and a few local tips
p: Forestry England describes Whinlatter as England's only true mountain forest, and once you are up among the trees it is easy to see why. The forest climbs high above the valley floor, so the air feels fresher and the views open up quickly, even on the shorter routes.

Keep your eyes on the branches as you walk. Whinlatter is one of the places in the Lake District where you have a decent chance of spotting red squirrels, which are a real treat now they have vanished from so much of England. Move quietly, look for nibbled cones on the path, and be patient.

For families, the play areas and trails around the visitor centre make an easy starting point, and younger walkers can tackle a short loop without anyone getting grumpy. More adventurous types can head higher for proper viewpoints, while the bike trails range from friendly blue routes to tougher red ones, so check the grading before you set off.

Allow anything from an hour for a quick wander to most of a day if you are biking or tackling the longer walks. The pass road is steep and twisty, so take it steady, especially in winter when the higher ground can be icy.

Coming down the hill, the village of Braithwaite sits at the foot of the pass with a couple of welcoming pubs. Carry on to Keswick for a lakeside walk along Derwentwater, a show at the Theatre by the Lake, or a short drive out to Castlerigg Stone Circle, which has one of the most dramatic settings of any ancient monument in the country.
